title: Add SpinQuant support for Qwen3.5 hybrid attention
body:
## Summary

Adds SpinQuant support for Qwen3.5, which uses a hybrid attention architecture
(a mix of full self-attention and linear / Gated DeltaNet layers). SpinQuant
previously had no mappings for this layout, so the modifier could not be applied
to Qwen3.5 models.

## Background

Qwen3.5 alternates full-attention layers (`q/k/v/o_proj`) with linear-attention
layers (`linear_attn.in_proj_qkv/z/b/a` + `linear_attn.out_proj`). The existing
SpinQuant mapping inference assumes a uniform self-attention layout, so it cannot
correctly identify the residual-stream read/write projections in the linear-
attention layers.

This change mirrors the dynamic-mapping approach already used by AWQ for hybrid
attention, generalized for SpinQuant.

## Changes

- **`spinquant/dynamic_mappings.py` (new)**: runtime mapping generation for dense
  hybrid-attention models.
  - Folds `linear_attn.in_proj_*` into `mlp_in` and `linear_attn.out_proj` into
    `mlp_out`, so R1 rotates the residual stream consistently across both
    full- and linear-attention layers.
  - Layer-index-restricted `input_layernorm` norm mappings so that full- and
    linear-attention layers each group exactly one norm per layer.
- **`spinquant/base.py`**: infer mappings via
  `get_spinquant_mapping_from_model` / `get_norm_mapping_from_model`; read the
  attention `head_dim` from `text_config` for heterogeneous configs.
- **`spinquant/mappings.py` / `spinquant/norm_mappings.py`**: move mapping
  inference out of the static registries; they now hold data only.
- **`utils/hybrid_attention.py`**: move `detect_linear_attn_projections` into a
  shared util, reused by AWQ (`awq/dynamic_mappings.py`).

## Why only R1 is supported

R2 rotates the value/output head space. Qwen3.5's full-attention layers apply an
element-wise gate (`attn_output * sigmoid(gate)`) between the attention output
and `o_proj`, inside that same head space, which does not commute with R2 and
breaks logits invariance. R3/R4 are online rotations and are unaffected by these
mappings. R1 alone preserves logits invariance (measured below).

## Testing

- Added unit tests for the dynamic mappings and fallback logic
  (`spinquant/test_dynamic_mappings.py`); updated AWQ's
  `test_dynamic_mappings.py` for the shared util move.
- Added an end-to-end R1 logits-invariance test on a tiny Qwen3.5 model
  (`spinquant/test_e2e_qwen3_5.py`), plus a `head_dim`-from-`text_config` test.
  **33 tests pass.**
- Verified R1 logits invariance on Qwen3.5-27B: MSE ≈ 1e-3 (below the existing
  SpinQuant correctness tolerance of 8e-3).

## Results (Qwen3.5-27B, WikiText-2 perplexity)

| method | PPL |
|---|---|
| baseline-fp16 | 6.4063 |
| rtn-fp8 | 6.4849 |
| rtn-w8a8 | 6.5804 |
| awq-w4a16 | 6.6177 |
| **spinquant-w4a16 (R1)** | **6.6233** |
| autoround-w4a16 | 6.7211 |
| smoothquant-w8a8 | 6.7306 |
| gptq-w4a16 | 6.9394 |
| rtn-w4a16 | 6.9595 |

SpinQuant W4A16 is data-free (no calibration data required) and matches AWQ W4A16,
which uses calibration data, while outperforming the other 4-bit methods.

title: Add WhisperForConditionalGeneration to AWQ mapping registry
body:
`WhisperForConditionalGeneration` had no AWQ mapping, so it silently fell back to `default_mappings`, whose balance layers (`q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`, `gate_proj`/`up_proj`, `down_proj`) never match Whisper's real layer names — its MLP is a plain `fc1`/`fc2` pair with no `gate_proj`/`up_proj`/`down_proj` at all, so smoothing was a complete no-op for this arch.

This mirrors `WHISPER_V2_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` (`smoothquant/utils.py`), which is already validated in production, translated into the `AWQMapping` dataclass shape:
- `self_attn_layer_norm` → `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `q_proj`
- `final_layer_norm` → `fc1`

**A scope note I want to be upfront about:** I deliberately did **not** add a `v_proj → out_proj` or `activation_fn → fc2` "second matmul" chain the way most other architectures here do (see `_bloom_mappings`' analogous `gelu_impl → dense_4h_to_h` entry for its own single-path MLP). Two things stopped me: Whisper's attention output projection is `out_proj`, not `o_proj`, and there's no existing evidence (SmoothQuant precedent or otherwise) this repo has validated such a chain for Whisper specifically — `_bloom_mappings`' own comment shows this kind of chain is sometimes deliberately excluded per empirical AutoAWQ findings, not a universal requirement. Happy to add it if you'd like, but didn't want to guess at something unverified. This PR also doesn't cover the decoder's cross-attention block (`encoder_attn` / `encoder_attn_layer_norm`), matching the existing SmoothQuant mapping's scope exactly.

TEST PLAN:
Constructed a tiny `WhisperForConditionalGeneration` on the meta device (no HF Hub download, no weight allocation) and confirmed empirically that the new mapping's regex matches its real `self_attn_layer_norm`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`/`q_proj`/`final_layer_norm`/`fc1` module names.

title: Roderick wu/better offload
body:
Changes to linearization, repacking, sequential pipeline offloading. 


## Implementation

### Sequential Pipeline Offloading
Removed the use of the offload context in the sequential pipeline. Onload/offload is manually managed now. 

Onloading is done as
```python
offload_kwargs = onload(subgraph_modules)
```
`subgraph_modules` is a hash as dict[str, module] where the key is the module's name. 
`offload kwargs` are in the form dict[str, dict]. Values are in the form returned by `get_cache_init_kwargs`

Offloading done as:
```python
offload(offload_modules, dict(offload_kwargs))
```

We do this so that we can swap out modules from the `subgraph_modules` when doing eager linearization/repacking easily. These operations create new module objects that need to be bound to the model. In addition, the old ones need to have all references deleted so that they can be freed, regulating our memory usage. 

Onload/Offload functions under `src/llmcompressor/pipelines/sequential/offloading.py`. 


We also add in prefetching for the onload/offload processes. Controlled by oneshot flag `sequential_module_prefetch`. This determines whether we overlap prefetching the next subgraph with the calibration/propagation process. 



We add flags `moe_eager_linearize_repack` (Linearize and/or repack each subgraph during calibration onload if `True`, linearize and/or repack before/after the whole model is calibrated for `False) and `repack_moe` (Whether or not to pack experts to 3d). 

Before calibration, we trace the whole model and build a hash for fast lookup for all moe modules -- packed or not packed. This is stored on the model as `model._moe_lookup`. Generated by `get_moe_linear_status`. 

This lookup is important because using model.get_submodules(name) traverses the whole model which is a taxing operation for large models. 

From here, we have functions as follows:
`linearize_moe_model`
`linearize_moe_subgraph`
`linearize_moe_layer`

and their corresponding repacking/reverse counterparts
`repack_moe_model`
`repack_moe_subgraph`
`repack_moe_layer`

The `*_model` functions are used with `sequential_linearize_repack=False`. They iterate over moe layers, onloading/offloading each layer individually (If you can't fit an entire moe layer on gpu at once, you're out of luck). The `*_subgraph` functions are assumed to be under a `disable_offloading_controlled` context. 

Some things to note:

Weird hard-to-read code such as:
```python
    linearized = [
        (moe_lookup[module], module)
        for module in subgraph_set
        if module in moe_lookup and isinstance(module, LinearExperts2D)
    ]

    for i in tqdm.tqdm(range(len(linearized)), desc="Repacking experts in subgraph"):
        repack_moe_layer(model, linearized[i][0], linearized[i][1])
```

Under these new contexts, since we want to constantly free up memory, we need to be careful with how we put out references. Iterating naively `for name, module in linearized` makes it such that linearized maintains a reference to the module. In the case that we are linearizing/repacking and the resulting new module is a new object, we want to free the old object. To my knowledge this can only be done when the python object is garbage collected. So here we make sure that the old module's reference is deleted by the end of its iteration. This is also why we need:

```python
        gc.collect()
        if torch.accelerator.is_available():
            torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
```

At the end of the new load context. We don't generate enough objects to force automatic garbage collection (at least for the tests I've run). The cache release might have a solution but I haven't been able to dig it up yet. Without that part it seems that we constantly have allocated but unused gpu memory.

title: [Observer] Triton grid search for the MSE observer
body:
## Summary

Adds a triton kernel for MSE observer

- remove compile path
- added a triton_error_buffer that works with patience. since the triton programs are per group, the native patience metric is much quicker to end the search compared to the eager mode's whole tensor patience. This makes accuracy much worse. To compensate we either have to get rid of patience for triton kernel [slow] or modify it so it is less aggresive. a 30% buffer seems to give approximately similar error/evaluation number characteristics. I tried various different patience numbers to align eager/triton behavior (e.g. 3x patience for triton or something like that) but it seems to behave a lot differently, resulting in more evaluations but worse accuracy unless the patience is set ridiculously high, in which case its just a lot more evaluations.
- triton kernel achieves bitwise parity with eager mode when patience/buffer are set to do full evaluation

benchmarks and kernel development: https://gist.github.com/HDCharles/51c392795d109078cb89b2f45ccfa11c

TODO: unify triton helpers between CT/LLMC

### Kernel details

The kernel uses buffered per-qparam patience and adaptive 512-value tiling:

- Small groups are packed so each Triton program handles roughly 512 values.
- Large groups are split into 512-value chunks, followed by a partial-error reduction.
- Candidate qparam calculation and QDQ are JIT-inlined helpers in `triton_utils.py`.
- INT, FP4, FP8, FP16/BF16/FP8 scale rounding, and E8M0 scales are supported.
- `triton_error_buffer` defaults to 100% for FP4 and 30% otherwise.
- The previous compile path and observer `chunk_size` setting are removed.

## Numerical parity

The packed BF16 NVFP4 path now reproduces eager arithmetic exactly, including:

- observed-dtype normalization before FP4 midpoint rounding;
- observed-dtype candidate min/max and scale rounding;
- observed-dtype `pow` inputs/results with FP32 reduction accumulation;
- host-precomputed FP32 grid points, avoiding reciprocal-rounding differences.

The deterministic expanded-NVFP4 Llama-3.1-8B output is bitwise identical to main. 

The exact-parity changes cost approximately 9-11% relative to the original adaptive prototype:

| Weight shape | Prototype | Parity kernel | Overhead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q/O projection | 8.324 ms | 9.100 ms | 9.3% |
| K/V projection | 2.333 ms | 2.579 ms | 10.6% |
| Up/Gate projection | 28.225 ms | 30.839 ms | 9.3% |
| Down projection | 28.230 ms | 30.860 ms | 9.3% |

for `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`

## End-to-end results

Expanded NVFP4 MSE example, `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`:

| Metric | Main eager | Triton parity | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full runtime | 335.65 s | 211.16 s | 1.59x |
| MSE grid search | 39.40 s | 3.73 s | 10.56x |
| Peak GPU allocated | 2.66 GB | 2.66 GB | same |
| Peak GPU reserved | 3.48 GB | 3.24 GB | 6.8% lower |

## Tests

Observer tests cover eager/Triton exact matching across INT4, FP4, FP8, tensor, channel, group, tensor-group and block layouts. A dedicated BF16 NVFP4 group-size-16 regression test exercises the packed path and its FP4 midpoint behavior.

title: [AutoRound] Pad captured inputs to a common sequence length
body:
## Purpose

Fix `test_ddp_smoke_autoround`, which regressed after `pad_to_max_length`
was changed to default `False` (#3180).

With that change, calibration samples are no longer padded to a fixed
`max_seq_length`. AutoRound batches calibration samples together and
concatenates the captured decoding-layer inputs along the batch dimension,
which requires every sample to share the same sequence length. With
variable-length samples this fails:

```
RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 0.
Expected size 512 but got size 436 for tensor number 3 in the list.
```

## Changes

Before handing captured inputs to AutoRound, right-pad them to the longest
captured sequence:

- `hidden_states`, `position_ids`, `position_embeddings` (`cos`/`sin`) and
  `cache_position` are padded along their sequence dimension.
- Attention masks are padded correctly by kind: integer padding masks with
  `0`, and float causal masks with the dtype minimum along the key
  dimension (so valid queries can't attend to pad keys) and `0` elsewhere.
- Per-sample validity masks (`[1, max_seq]`, zero on pad positions) are
  passed to AutoRound so pad positions are excluded from the tuning loss.

Right-padding is safe because causal attention prevents valid positions
from attending to trailing pad positions, so the reconstruction targets for
valid tokens are unchanged. When all captured samples already share a
length (e.g. `pad_to_max_length=True`), inputs are returned untouched and
the previous behavior is preserved.

## Testing

- Reproduced the failure with `oneshot(..., pad_to_max_length=False)` on
  `nm-testing/tinysmokeqwen3moe`; passes with the fix.
- `tests/llmcompressor/modifiers/autoround/test_base.py` and
  `tests/llmcompressor/transformers/autoround/test_autoround_oneshot.py`
  pass.

title: [Bugfix] Fix distributed hang from mis-shaped weight_global_scale writeback
body:
## Purpose

Fix a hang in distributed GPTQ caused by writing back an improperly formatted `weight_global_scale`.

## Background

In distributed GPTQ, each module is compressed on a single owning rank, which writes back its quantized weight and qparams via `update_offload_parameter`. That function updates an offload parameter **in place** (asynchronously) only when the new value matches the registered parameter's shape and dtype. When the shape/dtype does **not** match, it instead synchronously re-offloads a brand new parameter.

Previously the global scale was written as `global_scales[index].to(dtype=module.weight.dtype)` — a 0-dim tensor in the weight dtype — which does not match the registered `[1]` float32 `weight_global_scale`. Because only the owning rank performs this write, the ranks end up disagreeing on the parameter's shape/dtype, which stalls the collectives that later broadcast/save these params and hangs the run.

## Changes

- **`src/llmcompressor/modifiers/gptq/helpers.py`**: format the `weight_global_scale` writeback as a `[1]` float32 tensor (`global_scales[index].unsqueeze(0).to(dtype=torch.float32)`) so it matches the registered parameter and is updated in place on every rank.
- **`tests/.../gptq/test_gptq_ddp.py`**: new multi-GPU regression test that drives `GPTQModifier` directly (no `oneshot`) over the distributed compression path. It:
  - offloads a toy model to CPU with GPU onload to exercise the offload-cache writeback path,
  - uses a `tensor_group` float weight scheme (the case that produces `weight_global_scale`),
  - initializes the process group with a low NCCL timeout + blocking wait so any residual deadlock fails fast instead of hanging the suite,
  - asserts cross-rank `weight_global_scale` shape/dtype consistency and that broadcast quantized weights are identical across ranks.

## Testing

- `test_gptq_distributed_global_scale_writeback` passes with the fix (~14s).
- Reverting the source fix makes it fail deterministically (~3s) on the cross-rank shape assertion (`torch.Size([]) != torch.Size([1])`).

title: Fix split_fused_moe_experts for transposed MoE weights (Llama-4)
body:
## Summary

- `split_fused_moe_experts` assumes fused MoE expert weights are always stored as `[E, fused_intermediate, hidden]`, but Llama-4 uses a transposed layout `[E, hidden, fused_intermediate]`
- Without this fix, the split produces wrong-shaped tensors (e.g. `[2560, 16384]` instead of `[8192, 5120]`), which silently passes through model-free PTQ but errors at vLLM load time
- Detects the transposed format by reading `intermediate_size` from model `config.json` and comparing against the actual tensor dimensions — no shape heuristic needed
- Falls back to the `shape[2] > shape[1]` heuristic only when `moe_intermediate_size` is not provided (e.g. standalone callers outside the `model_free_ptq` pipeline)

## Repro

```python
import torch
from llmcompressor.entrypoints.model_free.process import split_fused_moe_experts

# Llama-4-Scout-like dimensions
num_experts, hidden, intermediate = 16, 5120, 8192

# Llama-4 stores experts transposed: [E, hidden, fused_intermediate]
tensors = {
    "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.gate_up_proj.weight": torch.randn(
        num_experts, hidden, 2 * intermediate, dtype=torch.float16
    ),
    "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.down_proj.weight": torch.randn(
        num_experts, intermediate, hidden, dtype=torch.float16
    ),
}

result = split_fused_moe_experts(tensors, moe_intermediate_size=intermediate)

# On main: gate_proj is [2560, 16384] — WRONG
# With fix: gate_proj is [8192, 5120] — correct
gate = result["model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.gate_proj.weight"]
assert gate.shape == (intermediate, hidden), f"got {gate.shape}, expected ({intermediate}, {hidden})"
```

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test `test_split_fused_moe_experts_transposed` — creates standard and transposed tensors, splits both with `moe_intermediate_size`, asserts identical shapes and values
- [x] Verified test fails on main and passes with fix

title: [Bugfix] Do not recurse into container modules in observe/update_qparams
body:
SUMMARY:

`observe()` and `update_qparams()` in `modifiers/quantization/calibration.py` decide whether their `module` argument is one module or a collection of modules with `isinstance(module, collections.abc.Iterable)`. Container modules are both: `nn.ModuleDict` is a `Module` *and* is `Iterable`, and iterating it yields its keys, which are strings. From there `observe("weight", ...)` iterates the string, `observe("w", ...)` iterates `"w"` back into `"w"`, and the recursion never terminates:

```
  File ".../llmcompressor/modifiers/quantization/calibration.py", line 99, in observe
    observe(m, base_name)
  [Previous line repeated 992 more times]
  File ".../llmcompressor/modifiers/quantization/calibration.py", line 97, in observe
    if isinstance(module, Iterable):
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<frozen abc>", line 119, in __instancecheck__
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded in comparison
```

Any model using `torch.nn.utils.parametrize` has such a `ModuleDict`, because torch stores parametrizations at `<module>.parametrizations`. The wav2vec2 family all do: wav2vec2, HuBERT, WavLM and UniSpeech-SAT weight-norm `encoder.pos_conv_embed.conv`.

Reproducer on `main` (28c9c76b), no downloads:

```python
import torch
from llmcompressor.modifiers.quantization.calibration import observe

model = torch.nn.Sequential(
    torch.nn.utils.parametrizations.weight_norm(torch.nn.Conv1d(4, 4, 1)),
    torch.nn.Linear(4, 4),
)
observe(list(model.modules()), "weight")  # RecursionError
```

**Scope, honestly.** On `main` neither in-tree caller trips this. `QuantizationModifier.on_sequential_epoch_end` and `GPTQModifier.on_sequential_epoch_end` both filter with `is_module_quantized` first, and a `parametrizations` `ModuleDict` has no `quantization_scheme`, so it never reaches `observe`. That filter arrived with #2784. On 0.12.0.x, where `on_event` passed `get_modules(parents)` straight through, it is a hard crash: `oneshot` on `microsoft/wavlm-large` with `QuantizationModifier(scheme="W8A16", targets=["Linear"], ignore=["classifier"])` dies with the traceback above (verified on 0.12.0.1). So on `main` this is a latent defect rather than a live crash — but the helpers are public and `QuantizationMixin` tells modifier authors to call them directly ("Modifier must explicitly call `observe(modules, base_name="weight")` then `update_qparams(modules, base_name="weight")`"), and the failure mode is a blown stack rather than an error message. The guard that hides it today lives in the callers, not in the helpers.

**Fix.** Check `Module` before `Iterable` so a container module is treated as a single module. `update_qparams` has the same dispatch and the same defect, so it gets the same treatment.

Two things worth calling out:

- This is a behaviour change for one case: passing an `nn.ModuleList`/`nn.Sequential` of quantized modules used to iterate it and now treats it as a single module, which is a no-op since containers carry no observers. No in-tree caller does that — callers pass a `list`, `dict_values`, or a single module — and the pipelines flatten with `.modules()`, so a container's children already arrive in the same list as separate entries.
- I fixed the helpers rather than filtering containers where the module lists are built (`Subgraph.submodules`, `list(model.modules())` in the basic/data-free pipelines), because there are several producers and only two consumers.

I did not add a `not isinstance(module, str)` guard: with the `Module` check in place nothing in-tree can produce a string here. Happy to add it if you would rather have the recursion hard-stopped regardless of caller.

Found while quantizing speech emotion classifiers (WavLM/HuBERT encoders with a classification head) to INT8/FP8/INT4. Our workaround on the released version is to fold the weight-norm parametrization away before `oneshot` and reapply it before saving.

TEST PLAN:

New test `tests/llmcompressor/modifiers/calibration/test_observers.py::test_observe_skips_container_modules`, which builds a weight-normed `Conv1d` next to a quantized `Linear` and runs `observe` + `update_qparams` over `list(model.modules())`, as the pipelines do. It is a real regression test on `main`:

```

$ pytest tests/llmcompressor/modifiers/calibration/test_observers.py::test_observe_skips_container_modules -q
```

title: [Datasets] Change `pad_to_max_length` default
body:
Previously `pad_to_max_length` defaulted to true, since SparseML was focused on fixed-size batched training. However, this is a bad policy now that the library is focused on calibration.

## Why this change revealed a latent bug

Flipping `pad_to_max_length` to `False` surfaced a pre-existing inconsistency in the sequential pipeline.

Sequential subgraphs are traced under **eager** attention (`trace_subgraphs` patches `_attn_implementation="eager"`). Eager attention bakes an *unconditional* causal-mask add into the traced graph:

```python
add_2 = mul_6 + wrapped_4   # wrapped_4 == create_causal_mask(...)
```

At calibration runtime, however, the model ran with its default attention implementation (e.g. `sdpa`). `create_causal_mask` under sdpa returns `None` for a fully-attending (all-ones) mask as an optimization — so the baked-in add becomes `Tensor + None` and raises:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'Tensor' and 'NoneType'
```

With `pad_to_max_length=True`, every calibration batch was padded to a fixed length, so the attention mask always contained padding zeros and `create_causal_mask` always returned a real tensor — accidentally hiding the trace/runtime mismatch. Once padding became dynamic, unpadded batches (all-ones mask) started returning `None`, exposing the bug. This reproduced via `tests/llmcompressor/observers/test_fused_observers.py::test_fused_observers_with_linear_sequential_targets`.

## Fix

Bake the eager-attention config patch into `calibration_forward_context` via a new `use_eager_attention` context manager, so tracing **and** runtime calibration always agree on the attention implementation. The now-redundant explicit patch in `trace_subgraphs` is removed.

title: [AWQ] Fix Qwen2.5-VL mapping registry entry (vision tower collapses MLP mapping)
body:
## Summary

`AWQ_MAPPING_REGISTRY` maps `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration` to `default_mappings`,
but those mappings do not resolve on this architecture — AWQ quantization fails outright:

```
ValueError: AWQ needs to match a single smoothlayer for each mapping but got
['model.language_model.layers.0.post_attention_layernorm',
 ...
 'model.language_model.layers.35.post_attention_layernorm']
for mapping: AWQMapping(smooth_layer='re:.*post_attention_layernorm$',
                        balance_layers=['re:.*gate_proj$', 're:.*up_proj$'])
```

This PR adds a VL-specific entry that keeps the two attention mappings unchanged and
scopes only the MLP mappings to the language model.

## Root cause

Qwen2.5-VL's vision tower (`model.visual.blocks.*`) names its MLP layers
`gate_proj` / `up_proj` / `down_proj` — the same names as the language model — but has
no `post_attention_layernorm`.

Measured on the real `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` module tree (839 modules):

| pattern | matches | where |
|---|---|---|
| `input_layernorm$` | 36 | language only |
| `post_attention_layernorm$` | 36 | language only |
| `q_proj$` / `k_proj$` / `v_proj$` / `o_proj$` | 36 each | language only |
| **`gate_proj$`** | **68** | **32 vision + 36 language** |
| **`up_proj$`** | **68** | **32 vision + 36 language** |
| **`down_proj$`** | **68** | **32 vision + 36 language** |

**Only the MLP names collide.** `default_mappings` balances
`re:.*post_attention_layernorm$` (36 language) against `re:.*gate_proj$` +
`re:.*up_proj$` (68 = 32 vision + 36 language). `match_modules_set` groups by shared
parent context, so the 32 vision blocks never close against a norm and the whole
resolution collapses into a **single group** instead of one group per decoder layer:

```
default_mappings' MLP entry → 1 group, sizes = [36, 68, 68]   # collapsed
```

AWQ's `_set_resolved_mappings` then sees 36 smooth layers for one mapping and raises.

Minimal reproduction: a 2-text-layer / 2-vision-block config is enough (`[2, 4, 4]`,
collapsed). A single-text-layer config does **not** collapse, because the smooth set has
one element and AWQ's guard is `len(smooth) > 1`.

## Fix

`_qwen2_5_vl_mappings` keeps all four `default_mappings` entries. The two attention
entries are byte-identical to `default_mappings` — they do not collide, so there is no
reason to touch them — and only the two MLP entries are scoped to the language model:

```
_qwen2_5_vl_mappings  →  4 mappings
  re:.*input_layernorm$                                          (unchanged)
  re:.*v_proj$                                                   (unchanged)
  re:.*language_model\.layers\.\d+\.post_attention_layernorm$     (scoped)
  re:.*language_model\.layers\.\d+\.mlp\.up_proj$                 (scoped)

→ 36 groups of [1, 1, 1] (and [1, 1] for the v_proj→o_proj entry)
```

The vision tower is excluded entirely rather than merely scoped out of the smooth set:
it is also excluded from quantization via the `ignore` list (keeping the vision encoder
in BF16 is the default for VLMs), so there is nothing for AWQ's balancing to compensate
for there.

### Why the patterns are not anchored at `model.`

The prefix is `re:.*language_model\.layers\.\d+\.`, not `re:model\.language_model\.…`.
transformers recently moved Qwen2.5-VL from `model.layers` + `model.visual` to
`model.language_model.layers` + `model.visual`, and llm-compressor supports a wider
transformers range than the one this was developed against. Anchoring at `.*` keeps the
pattern working across that rename. **Verified on transformers 5.14.1** — if the
supported floor is lower, the pattern may need adjusting there.

### Why a per-architecture mapping rather than a general fix

`match_modules_set` already accepts an `ignore` argument and `_set_resolved_mappings`
does not pass one. Threading AWQ's ignore list through would be the more general fix —
but `AWQTransformModifier` has no `ignore` field today (`mappings` / `duo_scaling` /
`n_grid` / `offload_device` only), so it means adding a field, wiring it through the
modifier lifecycle, and changing resolution behavior for **every** architecture.

**This PR is intended as the narrow fix; I'm happy to follow up with the general one.**
It is worth noting the same class of collision is not specific to Qwen2.5-VL: any VLM
whose vision tower uses SwiGLU-style MLP names is exposed (`Pixtral` /
`Mistral3` use `feed_forward.gate_proj`; Qwen3-VL is likely the same shape as 2.5-VL).
A general fix would cover those without a registry entry each.

## Testing

Added to `tests/…/awq/test_dynamic_mappings.py`, building a tiny
`Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration` on the **meta device** (no hub download, no weight
allocation):

- `test_vision_tower_collides_only_on_mlp_names` — asserts the property that makes the
  fix minimal: `gate_proj`/`up_proj`/`down_proj` hit both towers, while
  `input_layernorm` and the attention projections hit only the language model.
- `test_default_mappings_collapse_on_vl_tree` — pins the *bug*: asserts
  `default_mappings`' MLP entry collapses to one group and that the vision tower is what
  got pulled into the balance set. Fails if upstream fixes this another way, signalling
  that the registry entry can be dropped.
- `test_vl_mappings_resolve_one_group_per_layer` — asserts all **four** mappings resolve
  to one group per decoder layer, each target contributing exactly one module.
- `test_vision_tower_is_untouched_by_vl_mappings` — no `visual.*` module appears in any
  resolved group.
- `test_registry_points_to_vl_specific_mappings` — the registry entry is the new mapping,
  not `default_mappings`.

`make style` and `make quality` are clean on both changed files (with the repo's pinned
`ruff~=0.4.8`).

## End-to-end

On `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct`, AWQ W4A16:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| quantization | `ValueError` (collapsed) | completes (141 s) |
| checkpoint | — | 3.39 GB |
| loads in vLLM 0.29 | — | yes |

### Accuracy: does keeping the attention mappings matter?

DocVQA validation set, all 200 items, ANLS / exact-match:

| calibration | attention mappings | ANLS | exact |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_calib=128`, `n_grid=8` | dropped (earlier revision) | 0.9172 | 0.8350 |
| `n_calib=48`, `n_grid=6` | dropped | 0.8946 | 0.7600 |
| `n_calib=48`, `n_grid=6` | **kept (this revision)** | 0.8942 | 0.7550 |
| BF16 reference | — | 0.9217 | 0.8500 |

**At a matched calibration budget the two are indistinguishable** (ΔANLS 0.0004, Δexact 0.005).
On this benchmark I cannot measure a quality delta from the attention mappings in either
direction. The drop between the first two rows is the calibration budget, not the
mappings — the first comparison I ran changed both variables at once, and the controlled
row exists to correct that.

Keeping them is the right call regardless: silently dropping entries that
`default_mappings` prescribes changes how attention layers are smoothed, and that is not a
decision this PR should make implicitly.

### A note on calibration size

With all four mappings AWQ caches more activation statistics. `n_calib=128` thrashed this
16 GB card (stalled mid-grid-search at ~16.0 / 16.4 GiB with no progress); the runs above
use `n_calib=48`. Worth knowing if the mapping is validated on a small GPU.

## Related

- #2514 — same class of failure (`default_mappings` matching every layer's norm at once)
  on Qwen3.5 MoE, fixed by a per-architecture entry.

## Environment

```
llmcompressor 0.13.0 · compressed-tensors 0.18.0 · transformers 5.14.1
torch 2.13.0+cu130 · vLLM 0.29.0 · RTX 4080 SUPER (sm89)
```

title: Add GLM-5.3-MXFP4 checkpoint to What's New section
[AWQ] Drop padding at source and stream grid-search outputs
body:
## Background ##

AWQ's grid search holds three full copies of the calibration set's activations at once:

1. `_parent_args_cache` — the cached parent-module inputs
2. `fp16_outputs` — unquantized outputs, retained across all grid ratios
3. `int_w_outputs` — quantized outputs, rebuilt once per grid ratio

Padding tokens are carried through all of these and only discarded at the very end, inside `_compute_loss`:

```python
token_mask = loss_mask.to(fp16_batch.device) == 1
fp16_masked = fp16_batch[token_mask]
```

So padded positions contribute nothing to the loss, but a run with `pad_to_max_length=True` (the default) still pays for them in both memory and grid-search FLOPs.

This is not hypothetical. `examples/quantization_w4a16/qwen3_8_gptq_awq_example.py` OOMs on a single GPU. On `mlabonne/open-perfectblend` `train[:512]` with the Qwen3.8-27B tokenizer, mean sample length is 565 tokens against `max_seq_length=4096` — **7.2x** more tokens than needed. At `hidden_size=5120` in bf16 that is ~21.5 GB per copy, and `offload_device` defaults to `None` for non-MoE models, so it all sits in VRAM.

## Changes ##

* Add `_iter_sample_outputs`, which applies the loss mask as each batch's output is produced. Padding is dropped at the source instead of at loss time. `_run_samples` becomes a `list()` wrapper over it.
* `_compute_loss` now takes the module and streams the quantized outputs, accumulating MSE one batch at a time. This removes the `int_w_outputs` materialization from the grid-search loop, so peak memory holds a single batch rather than a second full copy of the calibration set.

Numerics are unchanged: masking is applied to exactly the same positions, and the per-batch accumulation order is preserved.

## Testing ##

* 43/43 existing AWQ unit tests pass
* Compared against `main` on `nm-testing/tinysmokellama-3.2` with `pad_to_max_length=True`: all 18 mappings produce **bitwise-identical** `best_scales` (max abs diff 0.0), and identical `initial_error`/`best_error` values

Not yet measured: an end-to-end peak-VRAM A/B. The reduction is argued from the code structure above rather than benchmarked, so that is worth confirming before this leaves draft.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR) ##

* The `_parent_args_cache` inputs are still padded and still on GPU for dense models. The `offload_device` default is gated on `is_moe_model()` (`base.py:182-194`), which is really a proxy for "the cache is big" — a dense 27B at 4096 tokens is exactly the case it misses. A size-based default would be better.
* Trimming padding from the cached inputs themselves is a larger win but needs care around padding side and attention semantics.

title: [Examples] Add Inkling-Small NVFP4/FP8_BLOCK example
body:
Adds a quantization example for `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small` under `examples/quantization_w4a4_fp4`:

- Loads the model with `device_map="auto_offload"` (disk offloading) since it does not fit in a single GPU
- Pins `moe_intermediate_size=2048` in the config, which the checkpoint's config.json omits (transformers would otherwise default to 3072 and hit a shape mismatch)
- Quantizes attention weights to FP8_BLOCK and mlp/MoE weights to NVFP4 via a single `QuantizationModifier`
- Saves in compressed-tensors format and copies the MTP tensors into the saved checkpoint via `save_mtp_tensors_to_checkpoint`

Existing Checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Inkling-NVFP4-FP8-BLOCK
